To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
iPP nanocomposites containing delaminated Co-Zn-Al LDH nanoparticles showed better flame retardancy and enhanced thermal stability compared to the iPP nancomposites made with two-metal LDHs.
the intralayer metals in LDH play a vital role in improving the flame-retardancy and thermal stability in the nanocomposites.
sonication-assisted delaminated Co-Zn-Al LDH, Zn-Al LDH, and sonication-assisted Co-Al LDH were used for the synthesis of iPP/Co-Zn-Al LDHy iPP/Zn-Al LDH and iPP/Co-Al LDH nanocomposites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the LDH metal constituents on the properties of polypropylene nanocomposites.
the influence of intralayer metal constituents of LDH on various properties of i-PP nanocomposites.
the preparation of polyolefin/LDH nanocomposite and the influence of the LDH on various properties of polyolefin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the three-metal LDH is a better candidate for the preparation of iPP nanocomposites for flame retardancy and improved thermal stability.
the type of LDHS has a significant influence on the thermal and flame-retarding properties of iPP nanocomposites.
the three-metal LDH containing iPP nanocomposites showed better thermal and flameretardant properties compared with the two-metal LDHS containing iPP nanoccomposites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the intralayer composition of LDH has no influence on the crystallization rate and storage modulus, but the thermal stability and flame-retardancy of the polypropylene/LDH nanocomposite are influenced by the intralayer LDH composition.

the LDH with the three-metal composition (Co–Z–Al LDH), which is the first time used as the filler material for the preparation of polyolefin nanocomposite, is a better choice for the polyolefin nanomaterials with improved flame-retardant, thermal, and crystallization properties.
the thermal and flame retardancy properties of polypropylene nanocomposites can be improved by incorporating LDH with three metals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LDHs can be used as a flame-retardant agent and that the flame-retardancy can be further improved by using a three-metal LDH.
the thermal stability and flame-retardancy properties of iPP can be enhanced with the incorporation of LDH nanoparticles.
the LDH intralayer metal constituents influence the flame retardancy of polypropylene.
